reviews.comment: I personally think that Dr. Rettenmaier was a good prof. His lectures could get a little boring, but the content was really interesting in my opinion. The project is easy, if you go to class he practically does the homeworks with you.  The final presentation was graded really easy as well.  Exams are not easy, just because of the amount of content.

Felt that I learned nothing about Poverty/Inequality in this class. Lectures are just abstract concepts about labor economics. There is a project that is almost a guaranteed A because he will walk you through it. Exams are really hard. Avoid this class if you actually want to learn about poverty and inequality.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the easier upper-level Econ classes at TAMU. Guaranteed a 100 on the HW and project because he shows you exactly how to do them and will almost do it for you during office hours. However, the lectures are painfully boring to listen to, and it is unclear exactly what you are supposed to glean from them. The midterm average was very low.

Be prepared to read lots of economic papers (no textbook required, assigned papers instead). Final grade is comprised of 2 exams, a final, quizzes, and a project. Unless you have prior excel knowledge, the project can be fairly confusing. He kind of just throws you into the ocean with no life jacket. If you go to class, you'll pass.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Rettenmaier's exams are more difficult than any I have taken so far in college. They require you to know absolutely everything about the topics he covers in class ranging from broad concepts and systems to small details such as the years of data used in a paper
